paragraphs: Apple sent invitations on Monday for a special event set for October 28, making official a product showcase that has been rumored for weeks.

While the company’s invitation didn’t reveal what’s on the agenda, it’s not difficult to guess. We can look forward to a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, new Macs powered by the latest Apple M6 processor, and an upgraded iPad mini.

Details of three unreleased Macs plus an iPad started leaking out months ago, pointing to a launch before the end of the year. More recently, an Apple event for October 28 was rumored. Now, the time for leaks and rumors is over.
“Can’t wait to pro and tell next week,” Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of worldwide marketing, wrote Monday on X.
At the same time, emails went out to the media, saying, “Please join us in person for a special Apple Experience in Los Angeles.” Apple scheduled the event for October 28 at 10 a.m. Pacific.

The biggest attraction at the October 28 Pro and Tell event could be Apple’s first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen. This will mark a major change — Apple resisted adding touch input to the Mac despite making it central to the iPhone and iPad.
Code changes in macOS 27 show Apple preparing to update the operating system to accommodate finger input without compromising its traditional desktop interface.

Rumors also point to redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch models with OLED displays, replacing the mini-LED technology used in current versions. OLED screens can deliver deeper blacks, stronger contrast and more vivid images. And a Dynamic Island-style cutout will apparently replace the new MacBook’s familiar display notch.
